lines: In educational testing, Differential Item Functioning (DIF) occurs when an item's statistical relationship to the latent trait $\theta$ differs between two groups after conditioning on ability level. An item with DIF is not merely harder for one group; it functions differently relative to what the group's overall ability would predict. The standard terminology refers to test-takers as ``examinees'' and questions as ``items.'' In our setting, examinees are LLMs and items are benchmark questions.

-The Mantel-Haenszel (MH) procedure~\citep{holland1988mh} detects DIF by stratifying examinees into $K$ score bins based on total score (a proxy for $\theta$) and computing a common odds ratio across strata. We use $K = 5$ equiprobable strata (quintile-based binning) following ETS recommended practice for large-scale assessments~\citep{donoghue1993mh,clauser1998dif}. Within each stratum $k$, the responses of the reference group and the focal group form a $2 \times 2$ contingency table:

+The Mantel-Haenszel (MH) procedure~\citep{holland1988mh,magis2010difr} detects DIF by stratifying examinees into $K$ score bins based on total score (a proxy for $\theta$) and computing a common odds ratio across strata. We use $K = 5$ equiprobable strata (quintile-based binning) following ETS recommended practice for large-scale assessments~\citep{donoghue1993mh,clauser1998dif}. \subsection{Temporal Comparability: 31\% Measurement Instability}
\label{sec:temporal}

\looseness=-1
We compare 2023 ($N = 1{,}080$) against 2024 ($N = 807$) models; 31.3\% of items receive ETS~C classification ($|\Delta_{\mathrm{MH}}| \geq 1.5$; 95\% bootstrap CI: [29.4\%, 38.1\%]; family-level cluster bootstrap CI $[26.7\%, 53.2\%]$). Three independent non-independence corrections converge on approximately 27--29\%: simple-mean DEFF correction (29.2\%), graduated family de-duplication at $K{=}20$ (29.1\%; \Cref{tab:lofo}), and family-level cluster bootstrap lower bound (26.7\%). The weighted-mean DEFF variant yields 13.5\%, but its effective cluster size ($\bar{m}{=}254$) implies each family member is functionally identical---unrealistic for models with distinct training data; with only ${\sim}$30 families, weighted-mean ICC estimates are unstable~\citep{valliant2013practical}. All reclassifications are significance-driven ($|\Delta_{\mathrm{MH}}| \geq 1.5$ unchanged); the $[13.5\%, 29.2\%]$ range reflects power uncertainty, not disagreement about DIF magnitude. We adopt ${\approx}$27--29\% as our primary corrected estimate, with 13.5\% as a conservative lower bound (\Cref{app:deff,app:uncertainty}). Even the most conservative bound exceeds the random-split baseline by $75\times$. Leave-one-family-out analysis confirms no single family drives the signal ($|\Delta\mathrm{C\%}| \leq 2.93$\,pp). C\% is stable across strata ($K \geq 5$: max $|\Delta\mathrm{C\%}| = 4.60$\,pp).

\looseness=-1
Three controls confirm genuine temporal change (\Cref{tab:temporal_landscape}): random splits yield C\% of 0.18\% (2023) and 1.3\% (2024), both ${\geq}23\times$ below temporal C\%; ability-quintile comparison yields 2.9\%; and 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching on total score ($N{=}638$/group, Cohen's $d = -0.17$) yields C\% $= 28.9\% \pm 0.1\%$, confirming at most ${\sim}2.4$~pp is attributable to ability mismatch ($p < 0.01$; \Cref{app:method_details}).

\looseness=-1

Looking at page 8 bottom, I can now see:
"6 Conclusion"
"Across six METABENCH benchmarks, 17.9-31.3% of items exhibit temporal measurement instability between 2023 and 2024 model cohorts (≈27-29% for MMLU after non-independence corrections; conservative bound: 13.5%). Web-overlap labels are near-independent of DIF flags (Jaccard = 0.206); rankings are preserved (ρ ≈ 0.997). We recommend MH-DIF audits at"

And then page 9 still has "≥500 models per cohort." at the very top.


The `\enlargethispage*{14\baselineskip}` in discussion.tex is already maxed out—pushing it to 15 causes float oscillation—so I need to try a different approach, maybe combining a smaller enlargement with negative vspace adjustments to fit the conclusion properly. I'm considering merging the final sentences of the conclusion to avoid awkward line breaks, though that won't actually reduce the character count. A better strategy might be using `\looseness=-2` to force TeX to compress the paragraph more aggressively than `\looseness=-1` would.

But I should verify whether the current looseness setting is even having an effect—if the paragraph naturally renders at five lines and the looseness parameter isn't reducing it, then pushing it further won't help. Instead, I could try `\emergencystretch` to give TeX more flexibility in spacing.

Actually, the simplest fix is to just cut the audit recommendation from the end since it's already covered in section 5.2, leaving only the Jaccard independence result and ranking preservation statement.

Though removing the recommendation entirely makes the conclusion feel incomplete. I could keep a shorter version—something like "temporal DIF audits should accompany score reporting" or "motivating temporal MH-DIF audits"—that's brief enough to avoid the overflow while still pointing forward.
